stories.headline: Steelers Aaron Rodgers, QB room lead NFL Week 7's best arrivals
stories.summary: NFL stars continue to turn game-day arrivals into their own weekly fashion showcase.
stories.body:
Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback room set the fashion standard high Sunday in Paris, simulating European-style looks from their favorite show "Peaky Blinders" with three-piece suits and flat caps.

The idea spawned from backup quarterback Mason Rudolph, who reached out to clothing designer Mitch Purgason to have the suits custom-made for this game.

Rudolph explained that the Steelers quarterback room bonds over "Peaky Blinders." The show is extremely British, not French. But Rudolph's idea was to lean into United Kingdom experience and display with energy that they connect with personally.

Purgason said he flew up to Pittsburgh to custom-fit the Steelers quarterback room 13 days ago, then he and his associate stylist, Rachel Leskowsky, went to work making the suits in about nine days. Purgason then flew up to hand-deliver the fits last minute before their flight to Paris.

The work is worth it for looks as clean as the Steelers quarterback room. They posed for pregame pictures in Paris, and it exuded boss energy. Will this lead to more NFL positional groups leaning into translating their personal connection niche into fashion?

Here are Week 7's most fashionable NFL player gameday fits that caught our eye:

Sunday's best
It was tracksuits galore in the afternoon slate, with Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald styling a black look with a pair of shades. Meanwhile, Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby broke out a white jumpsuit, showing off his ink with an unzipped jacket.

Though Sunday marked a holiday in National Tight Ends Day, that didn't stop Rodgers and the Steelers quarterback room from channeling their inner "Peaky Blinders" in Paris with coordinated suits, boots, flat cap and all.

Thursday's looks
Caleb Williams kept it sharp ahead of "Thursday Night Football," pairing a navy suit with a black crewneck shirt. The Chicago Bears quarterback skipped the tie but not the wired earbuds. Naturally, he had his matcha drink in one hand and a structured brown leather bag in the other.

stories.headline: United States Grand Prix LIVE! F1 race updates in Austin, commentary and results
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli starts the United States Grand Prix on pole position from Max Verstappen.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli has edged closer to sealing his first drivers' world championship as he starts on pole for the United States Grand Prix, and you can follow live updates on ESPN.

The Mercedes driver beat Red Bull's Max Verstappen to the line by 0.179 seconds.

- Kimi Antonelli takes pole in bid to seal world title at United States Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli ecstatic with first pole since July at United States GP: 'It's good to be back'

Verstappen's teammate Isack Hadjar will line up on the second row in third, with Charles Leclerc in the Ferrari behind.

Lewis Hamilton, despite finishing fastest in final practice, was down on the timesheets and will start fifth.

George Russell couldn't find the pace as Mercedes continue to work on unlocking the new upgrades and was sixth-fastest.

Antonelli can seal the title at the Circuit of the Americas in Austin if Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Russell finishes ninth or lower.

The title leader said after securing his first pole since July: "Yeah, I mean, we've got pole, so we'll try to win tomorrow. But Max has been very quick, and also, Isack did an incredible job in qualifying.

"It's not going to be easy, but we'll try to get a good start, and then hopefully we'll lead into Turn 1, and then we'll try to set the pace, even though it's going to be very tight. But very happy with the qualifying today. Q3 was very tough with the wind, very gusty, unpredictable, but happy that we stuck it on pole."

stories.headline: Time, place unclear for Game 6 of Valkyries-Dream WNBA Finals
stories.summary: With the Valkyries forcing a Game 6 in the WNBA Finals, the Dream are working to resolve a scheduling issue that leaves the venue and time of the game up in the air.
stories.body:
After the Valkyries beat the Dream 67-62 in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday in Atlanta's State Farm Arena, tying the best-of-seven series at 2-2, one question was answered and another far more important question was raised.

There will be a Game 6 in Atlanta. But nobody knows where or even when the game will be played despite a furious round of negotiations spilling into Sunday between the WNBA, NBA, Valkyries, Dream and Atlanta Hawks, sources told ESPN.

The Dream -- whose home venue of Gateway Center Arena has a capacity of approximately 3,500 -- have played all five home playoff games at the 17,000-seat State Farm Arena, home to and operated by the Hawks. Coordination between the leagues, teams and multiple media partners resulted in Games 3 and 4 of the Finals getting moved to State Farm Arena. Game 3 was shifted up a day, from Thursday to Wednesday, while the Hawks agreed to hold a doubleheader with the Dream and moved tip time of Saturday evening's home opener back 30 minutes.

But with the Hawks hosting the Cleveland Cavaliers at State Farm the night of Game 6, along with other scheduling complications, the situation is more complex than what the leagues dealt with earlier in the series and could have millions of dollars of impact on both leagues.

"We continue to explore all options," a WNBA spokesperson told ESPN.

Said a Dream spokesperson: "We are waiting to hear from the league if any changes can be made to allow us to play in State Farm Arena. If not, the game will be played in Gateway Center Arena."

Sources believe it's a real possibility that Game 6 will be held Thursday as scheduled at Gateway Center Arena in College Park.

"There are problems with all the solutions," one source close to the situation said.

Sources told ESPN that the NBA has been working with the Hawks and Cavaliers to determine if Thursday's game could be switched to an alternate date -- or even to Cleveland. While some stakeholders feel the onus should be on the NBA to move its regular-season game so the WNBA Finals can be prioritized, there has been pushback from others that the domino effects of moving that game are too complicated.

Thursday's Cavaliers-Hawks game is already a back-to-back for both teams: The Hawks host the Miami Heat at State Farm Arena on Wednesday, when the Cavaliers play a home game before traveling to Atlanta.

Moving Thursday's game to Cleveland is a radical idea that has been discussed, sources said, but it would create a home-road back-to-back for the Hawks in addition to the logistical nightmare of scheduling a new home game in Cleveland with just a few days' notice.

Following Thursday's game, Cleveland is supposed to play Saturday in Milwaukee, which could also be hosting Game 7 of the World Series. Fridays are NBA Cup exclusive games, while Hawks-Cavaliers is a non-Cup game.

State Farm Arena has open dates on Tuesday -- the day after Golden State hosts Game 5 -- and Friday. One proposal would move Game 6 of the WNBA Finals to Friday and Game 7, if necessary, from Saturday, Oct. 31, at Chase Center to Tuesday, Nov. 3.

The WNBA would support that proposal, but only if both teams agree to it, sources said.

The Valkyries have raised concerns about moving two WNBA Finals games and the three off days that proposal would create in between Games 5 and 6 as well as between Games 6 and 7, sources said.

"We're proud to be part of such a compelling Finals and love seeing the growth of the game," a Valkyries spokesperson said in a statement. "We fully support what's best for the league and will stand behind whatever it decides."

Playing Game 7 on Nov. 3 would conflict with a recent NBA policy of not holding games on Election Day, although sources said that does not currently appear to be a strong concern.

Availability at Chase Center is also not abundant. The Golden State Warriors -- whose ownership group also owns the Valkyries -- have home games scheduled against the LA Clippers on Sunday, Nov. 1, and Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2.

While they don't share an ownership group with the Dream, the Hawks have expressed a desire to help facilitate the WNBA Finals in their arena, as they did for Games 3 and 4, sources said. The Dream will be a full-time tenant at State Farm Arena beginning in 2027, the team announced earlier this month, which should make holding playoff dates in the future more seamless.

There has been discussion about moving Thursday's game to a matinee, like Game 4 was, sources said. The Hawks have been open to facilitating another doubleheader at State Farm Arena, but other sources said the WNBA believes the idea of a weekday matinee for a Finals game would not be as desirable compared to a weekend matinee.

Other Atlanta-area alternate arenas -- such as Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion or Gas South Arena in Duluth -- aren't viewed as ideal since they would feel like road games for both teams.

Games 3 and 4 in Atlanta sold out quickly once they were moved to State Farm Arena. Fans wanting to purchase tickets for Game 6 have been told to wait for a resolution to the scheduling conflicts, sources said.

While it is not uncommon for WNBA playoff games to be moved to alternate sites because of arena commitments to NBA games or other events, sources on all sides of this situation expressed frustration that these issues hadn't been resolved before Saturday.

"This should've been solved weeks ago, and definitely at the same time Games 3 and 4 were solved," one source said.

Said another: "The fact we are making these decisions so we can play a WNBA game at a larger arena is the best news of all. ... It just has to be scheduled better in advance. Moving games is much harder now than it would have been a week ago."

stories.headline: Sunderland stay bottom of PL table after goalless draw with Leeds
stories.summary: Sunderland and Leeds were forced to share the spoils in a goalless stalemate at the Stadium of Light.
stories.body:
Sunderland and Leeds were forced to share the spoils in a goalless stalemate at the Stadium of Light.

A scrappy first half saw Brian Brobbey have two promising opportunities to put the Black Cats ahead but he was denied both times by James Trafford.

Both sides threatened after the break and Nilson Angulo enjoyed the better chances for Sunderland before Ao Tanaka came close for the visitors.

A point snaps the Wearsiders' four-game losing run in the Premier League but they remain bottom of the standings, while Leeds stay in the top half of the table, sat seventh.

Brobbey made his return from injury with a place in the starting line-up as one of six changes from Sunderland's midweek Europa League draw against Lech Poznan and Daniel Farke made three switches to the side who drew 1-1 with Manchester United last weekend.

Leeds sniffed around the Sunderland box in the early stages as Jayden Bogle skewed wide and Harry Wilson's free-kick was met by Jaka Bijol, but his flicked header was easily held by Robin Roefs.

The Black Cats had an excellent opportunity to take the lead when Brobbey fired towards the bottom left corner, forcing Trafford into a low save.

Brobbey was in the thick of the action again, pouncing on the ball following a tame exchange of passes between the Leeds defence, and Trafford was quick off his line to block the striker's shot.

The chance spurred Sunderland on as they enjoyed a bright spell around the Leeds box, but neither side was able to put a shot away as the half petered out.

A bizarre incident at the start of the second half saw Nordi Mukiele caught around the throat by team-mate Luke O'Nien and the defender was forced off, with Omar Alderete replacing him seven minutes after the restart.

The centre-half was immediately called into action to clear a dangerous Leeds delivery into the area and Sunderland were forced to scramble away an overhead kick attempt from Brenden Aaronson.

Tarik Muharemovic's header from a corner was held by Roefs as Leeds continued to pile on the pressure.

Angulo had a fierce effort pushed away by Trafford and minutes later the winger was again denied by a diving save from the Leeds goalkeeper.

An inswinging corner from Granit Xhaka was cleared as far as Angulo, who had another effort blocked for the Black Cats.

Leeds broke through substitute Anton Stach down the middle and a cross from Bogle on the right was hooked away at the back post by Noah Sadiki.

Tanaka's shot was stopped by Roefs and O'Nien and Dominic Calvert-Lewin raced for the loose ball, which was eventually cleared.

A mistake at the back nearly allowed Chemsdine Talbi through, but the substitute's strike was blocked by Bijol.

In the final minutes, Sean Longstaff was denied by a low stop from Roefs and the midfielder had a strike blocked by bodies in front of the goal line as the points were shared.

stories.headline: Sunday's fantasy basketball adds and bets to make in the NBA
stories.summary: Jim McCormick breaks down Sunday's slate, highlighting the fantasy streamers to add and bets to make.
stories.body:
ESPN's basketball daily cheat sheet is your pregame destination before you lock in daily fantasy and betting decisions for that night's games. Here you'll find our top insights for the slate, including players to target for your daily fantasy rosters, along with game-by-game injury reports.

What you need to know for Sunday
A seven-game Sunday slate features a series of potential competitive contests. Only one game on the docket claims a double-digit point spread -- a departure from a Saturday field that was full of large lines. The marquee matchup of the day features the Minnesota Timberwolves hosting the Toronto Raptors in a meeting of deep, darkhorse contenders.

Close games bode well for developing fantasy and betting angles, as rotations and workloads prove more predictable in competitive games. A good place to start during a busy day of basketball is the injury report, which tells us that we won't see Paolo Banchero, Zach Edey or Jalen Duren playing for their respective teams. Joel Embiid, meanwhile, is set to rest for the second leg of a back-to-back series for the Philadelphia 76ers.

While we're still learning how each rotation and coaching staff will react to the absence of big names from the gameplan, we can proactively make some decisions based on precedent and prediction.

For the Orlando Magic, a proven veteran big man is due for more minutes and work in the wake of Banchero's ankle injury, as you'll read below. What will Memphis do sans Edey? How will Detroit cope with being sans their interior anchor in South Philly tonight?

And, those 76ers don't have a one-to-one backup for Embiid like they did in seasons past in the form of Andre Drummond. They will instead likely turn to a collective and small-ball looks -- possible even some featuring LeBron at center. We'll learn a lot today about all of these sides, which can serve us in future slates, as well.

With an eye toward uncovering compelling betting angles and fantasy decisions, let's take a look at the day ahead in the NBA.

Fantasy stream team -- widely available players worth adding
Wendell Carter Jr., C, Orlando Magic (rostered in 23.5% of ESPN leagues)
With Banchero in street clothes for tonight's tilt with the New York Knicks, Carter should see more minutes, rebounding chances, and post touches as a result. The Knicks lack the interior defense and rebounding from last season's run, supporting confidence in double-double upside for this veteran big.

Paul Reed, C/PF, Detroit Pistons (14.2%)
Assuming Philadelphia decides to rest Embiid in the second game of a back-to-back, they will likely turn to a number of different looks to cover for him. Reed, who will consume a good bit of the work reserved for Duren, would then be facing a 76ers lineup badly lack rebounding acumen, establishing a nice floor for this active and unique frontcourt talent. It also helps that there is a fun narrative in play, as "B-ball Paul" began his career in Philly.

Egor Demin, PG/SG, Brooklyn Nets (48.3%)
The Nets haven't had many promising prospects in this recent era of drafting. Demin represents the closest thing to a rising playmaker, as he's capable of creating for both himself and others. Such a skill set is rare for this Nets group, which helps Demin project as a rewarding pickup for today's matchup with the uptempo Indiana Pacers.

Jalen Suggs, PG/SG, Magic (31.3%)
Independently valuable as a two-way guard when he's hot from the field, Suggs flashed more offense in Game 2 of the season and should take on more work today with the team's top star missing. Suggs can deliver a fun fantasy line even without much scoring, which is nice when looking to finish out the fantasy week in category formats.

Jim's bets to make on Sunday
Walker Kessler OVER 26.5 combined points and rebounds

Revenge narratives are usually overblown, but this setup -- with Kessler facing the Utah Jazz -- proves intriguing. The Jazz, without their incumbent starting center Jusuf Nurkic, are exposed to rebounding gaps and rim protection issues. Enter Kessler, who has thrived as a lob threat and rebounder on both sides of the floor as a Laker.

Jaylen Brown OVER 6.5 rebounds (-117)

Brown -- and not Embiid or LeBron James -- paces the 76ers with 13.5 rebounding chances per game this season. This is defined as being the closest player to the basketball at any point between when the ball crosses below the rim and when the rebound is completely secured. This seems good for potential rebounding success (assuming Embiid's absence) and no Duren cleaning the glass. Brown plays big minutes and spends time crashing the glass. Sign me up.

Wendell Carter Jr. OVER 7.5 rebounds (-109)

Building on the endorsement of "WCJ" as a fantasy streamer, his rebounding opportunities should spike with Banchero sidelined. Banchero, after all, leads the team in rebounding chances per game, even having missed time in the team's most-recent game. While the Knicks still have solid rebounding talent and scheme in their favor, Carter's mix of minutes, talent, and positioning support optimism for his rebounding results.

stories.headline: Who is this year's Mr. October? Tracking the playoff MVP for 2026
stories.summary: We go inside the numbers on the players doing the most to help their teams win.
stories.body:
Who is hero of the 2026 MLB playoffs?

To try to answer to that question, we're tabulating the cumulative win probability added figures for every player in the postseason. But we've added a twist: The deeper we get into the playoffs, the more weight the WPA carries. The division series counts double the wild-card round, then we'll double it again for the championship series and, finally, once again for the World Series.

This means that players who shine in the early rounds can still get on the leaderboard, but it's more difficult. Coming through when the championship leverage is at its highest is what becoming an October hero is all about.

Saturday's hero: Forget Sal Frelick's offensive numbers. The guy is a folk hero in Milwaukee. This was true before Saturday, but it's reached Bunyanesque proportions after Frelick smacked a game-tying homer in the sixth inning of Game 2. That evened the score at four and completed the Brewers' comeback from a four-run deficit. Frelick's fourth-inning single also contributed to the Brewers' third run. There were a lot of big momentum swings in Game 2, but nothing got the ballpark rocking like Frelick's blast.

Methodology
As mentioned above, each player's win probability added (WPA) is tracked on a per-game basis. Each round of the playoffs counts double that of the previous round. The tabulation is then converted to an AXE-style index in which 100 represents the average for all postseason players. The "Change" column looks in the changes in AXE numbers from the previous day for players who were in action. You can sort this column by clicking on it to see the day's heroes.

stories.body:
After Saturday's dozen contests, the NHL offers a smaller slate Sunday, but there are some captivating matchups on the docket.

That includes the Heritage Classic -- the All-Canadian outdoor matchup held at Princess Auto Stadium in Winnipeg this season -- along with some interconference pairings and a GM taking on his old team. (Well, he's not ... but his new team is. You get it.)

Here's a look at what you need to know for each game, including betting info and broadcast details:

Odds are provided by DraftKings and subject to change.

Florida Panthers at Chicago Blackhawks

3 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | FLA -180, O/U: 6.5

Spencer Knight revenge game? The Connecticut native served as Sergei Bobrovsky's backup during the early part of his career but was traded to the Blackhawks in March 2025 as part of the package for Seth Jones. The Panthers would go on to win another cup that spring, while Knight is now backstopping Chicago through an ongoing rebuild.

The Panthers started the season 5-2-1 (including an OT win over the defending champs on opening night) but have lost two straight by an aggregate score of 9-1. Meanwhile, the Blackhawks are 2-2 since Connor Bedard's return this season. Which side earns the vital two points in this one?

New York Islanders at Dallas Stars

6 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | DAL -198, O/U: 5.5

Peter DeBoer revenge game? After guiding the Stars to three straight Western Conference finals appearances, the coach was unceremoniously dumped in the 2025 offseason. This will be his first game against his former team since that split.

But beyond that narrative, this could also feature a matchup between two of the NHL's top goaltenders: Dallas' Jake Oettinger (5-2-1, with a 1.23 goals-against average and .939 save percentage) and New York's Ilya Sorokin (5-2-0, 1.72, .934). And in front of those tenders, two of the game's elite defensemen will be plying their trade: Miro Heiskanen of the Stars and Matthew Schaefer of the Isles.

Montreal Canadiens at Winnipeg Jets

7 p.m. ET (TNT) | MTL -122, O/U: 5.5

As the teams head outdoors to skate in front of thousands of very cold fans, neither is in playoff position; that's perhaps not a surprise for the Jets, who had modest expectations, but it's shocking for the Habs, who some believe to be the best team in the Atlantic.

So we'll see how this game plays out between these two teams (in their special uniforms). Also of note: This is the first game the Jets will play following the Connor Hellebuyck trade; he had not suited up for them this season, but perhaps the psychological burden of the uncertainty will be lifted?

Colorado Avalanche at Nashville Predators

8 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | COL -230, O/U: 6.5

Chris MacFarland revenge game? Well, that's a stretch. The new Predators GM left the Avs on his own accord -- and then made some notable trades with his former boss Joe Sakic, including acquiring Jack Drury and Ross Colton among others heading in both directions.

To no one's surprise, the Avs are right in the mix for a playoff spot, while the Preds are a few points back. Do they make up any ground here -- and do Drury and Colton make the difference?

Minnesota Wild at Vancouver Canucks

10 p.m. ET (ESPN+) | MIN -180, O/U: 6.5

Canuck fans revenge game? Here's what Greg Wyshynski had to say in citing this as a must-see game in the Wysh List this week:

"Now that we've seen how Ottawa fans have greeted the return of a former captain who was traded to play with his brother after informing his team he wasn't going to sign a new contract with them, Quinn Hughes plays in Vancouver for the first time following those exact circumstances. Well, save for the whole 'playing with his brothers' thing. That comes later."

On paper, this does not look like a very close game -- but we'll make note here that these very same Wild lost 2-1 to the Flames on Thursday, and they'll be skating in this one 24 hours after taking on the surprising Kraken.

stories.headline: Bayern Munich's Vincent Kompany 'stable,' could be away for weeks after collapse
stories.summary: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will have more tests to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.
stories.body:
Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany will undergo more testing to determine why he collapsed during a training session the previous day, the club said Saturday.

Board member for sport Max Eberl told reporters that Kompany's condition was "stable" and that doctors were focused on "trying to find out" the cause.

"The tests have already yielded some results, but further results are needed to determine exactly what it is and how long it will take for him to recover," Eberl said.

Kompany, 40, was observing a training session for the reserves team when the incident occurred Friday.

Kompany had been dealing with a viral infection since last week, and his assistant Aaron Danks said on Tuesday it affected the Belgian's legs.

Kompany remained seated throughout Bayern's 6-1 win over Leipzig last week and then missed a training session and a pregame news conference on Tuesday, when Danks said he needed time to rest at home.

However, Kompany returned to the dugout for Wednesday's 2-2 draw against Arsenal in the Champions League. Following that match, Kompany acknowledged he tried to push through the illness and failed to heed the signals from his body.

Eberl said that he spoke to Kompany and his wife on Friday after Kompany collapsed.

- Bayern's Kompany hospitalized after collapsing at training

The executive added that as of now there was no time frame for when Kompany would return, saying it could take weeks.

"He'll only come back when he's fit," Eberl said. "We're not going to start setting any time frames. We need to find out what the issue is, and then it's a question of what the recovery time will be. We're not talking in terms of days, but weeks."

Kompany, a former player, joined Bayern in 2024 from Burnley and has won the German league twice since then. Kompany's team also reached the Champions League semifinals and won the German Cup last season.

He is nominated for the Johan Cruyff Trophy for the best coach of the year to be announced Monday.

Bayern will visit Freiburg in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

stories.headline: Consensus top AFL draft prospect Dougie Cochrane already in rare air
stories.summary: Missing significant chunks of football hasn't stopped Port Adelaide NGA star Dougie Cochrane from firming as the top prospect in this year's AFL Draft.
stories.body:
It's rare for a player to be the consensus no. 1 rated prospect in their draft. From coaches to recruiters and a myriad of draft evaluators, Dougie Cochrane stands atop 2026's crop. For him to do so after playing just four games in his top-age campaign puts the Port Adelaide NGA gun in rare air.

The starring junior missed both years of his u18 national championships through injury, and this year only returned to the field in the final month of the season. But what he produced at league level last season and amongst his peers at the u16s national championships in 2024 is not easily forgotten.

Clearly a class above at the national championships three years ago, Cochrane put all of his skill and athleticism on show. He was a distributor out of defence, won aerial duels around the ground and was the focal point of the SA forward line in a showing of his unique versatility.

From there he made his league debut for Central Districts as a 17-year-old, kicking four goals including an outrageous snap on his left foot from the pocket after crumbing a forward 50 contest. From his first game he was already the best player on the ground.

Speaking to ESPN ahead of the draft combine Cochrane was a bit flat. It wasn't because he'd missed his top-age season, he knew he wasn't going to be testing, and he knew most clubs wouldn't bother booking an interview given his ties to Port Adelaide. But there was one thing that really got to him.

"They measured me at 194-and-a-half centimetres," he tells ESPN with a grin. "They took a centimetre off me, but we'll round that up."

At six-foot-four (we'll round it up too) he's widely considered the next elite key forward prospect to come through the AFL Draft. Only he doesn't necessarily see it that way.

"I want to be a midfielder when I'm older, that's what I'm striving towards. "For right now I'm pretty happy forward, if not back. I'm happy wherever the team needs, whatever the team needs.

"I'm pretty skinny right now, I'm not as muscly as the Patty Cripps's of the world, the Bonts of the world. I want to focus on my midfield craft and get that experience."

Cochrane missed a significant chunk of his bottom-age year with a hamstring and over the off-season underwent knee surgery to address patella tendinitis. He didn't play for 11 straight months from the end of 2025 to July 2026.

Watching from the sidelines frustrated him but he knew it was all out of an abundance of caution.

"I started playing league at Centrals last year, I sort of started feeling [knee pain] a little bit. I thought nothing of it, just thought it was a bit of growing pain. It got worse and worse by the time I started doing pre-season... when you take off and do your powerful stuff it flares up.

"They did a clean out of it... I had the surgery, and I walked out of the surgery. It was two little key holes."

Cochrane sat down with ESPN as Port Adelaide list manager Jason Cripps all but confirmed on Trade Radio Essendon would be bidding on the gun academy prospect at pick one in the 2026 AFL Draft.

He's the son of Port Adelaide and North Melbourne midfielder Stuart Cochrane, and grew up supporting the Power after his dad's playing career finished up. His brother Tom was on the list during formative years and the club is set up to match his bid wherever it lands.

"Dad's been my idol growing up. Looking up to him, I obviously didn't get to see him play but he's been enormous."

Asked if it would mean more being that first selection on November 19, Cochrane's humble nature shines through.

"I loved watching the draft growing up, seeing those high picks. The pick doesn't really matter, does it? There have been a lot of picks over times where the number one picks haven't gone as well as they should've. I just want to end up at an AFL club - wherever that is I don't mind - but I just want to play footy," he says.

"Growing up and supporting Port all my life, it would be special playing for them. But whatever happens happens and I'm just gonna let that decide itself."

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at United States GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- Kimi Antonelli takes pole in bid to seal world title at United States Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli ecstatic with first pole since July at United States GP: 'It's good to be back'

- Max Verstappen taking painkillers to deal with 'impossible' bumps at United States Grand Prix circuit

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin have now increased after he put his Mercedes on pole for the seventh time this season. Antonelli would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower. Hamilton will line up on the grid in fifth, while Russell is behind in sixth.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Brighton's Fabian Hürzeler digs at Liverpool - 'one team' tried to create
stories.summary: Brighton & Hove Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler appeared to take a swipe at Liverpool's approach in their 2-0 win over his side at Anfield, claiming there was "one team" who tried to create.
stories.body:
Brighton & Hove Albion boss Fabian Hürzeler appeared to take a swipe at Liverpool's approach in their 2-0 win over his side at Anfield, claiming there was "one team" who tried to create.

An own goal from Pascal Gross and a neat finish from Alexander Isak were enough to seal the victory for Andoni Iraola's side.

However, Brighton ended the afternoon having enjoyed more possession and generated a higher expected goals (xG) tally than their opponents -- something Hürzeler was quick to point out in his postmatch news conference.

"I think everyone in the stadium saw that there was one team who really tried to create and try to win this game and therefore I have to praise my players," the Brighton boss said.

"I think everyone in the stadium, and you as well, felt there was a missed opportunity for us, because it's not only after the goal or the goals they scored.

"Also, before they scored, we had one, two big chances and today I think it was just the difference that they scored, we didn't score. They kept a clean sheet because they defended well with their centre-backs, with full-back [Ronald] Araujo and with [Milos] Kerkez.

"I think they blocked a lot of shots. They really defended the box well. We didn't have that efficiency. We couldn't keep the clean sheet because we made easy mistakes, we lost some important personal duels.

"But overall I saw a team with a lot of good things to take away. I saw a team that really had the belief in our approach, that stuck to the match plan, that always kept going, and that is very frustrating because we all have the feeling that there is a missed opportunity here today."

- Iraola era at Liverpool finally has liftoff thanks to big-money forwards

- Michael Carrick pressure grows, Bournemouth run riot at Man United

- Man City must be 'more clinical,' Enzo Maresca demands

Meanwhile, Liverpool enjoyed their fourth victory in a row in all competitions under Iraola, with the Reds moving up to fourth in the Premier League table.

"I'm very happy," Iraola said.

"I'm happy with this fourth win [in a row].

"I think today we had a very good opposition in front of us, similar to Villarreal the other day -- teams that are technically really good. I think today the key was how we started. We needed a strong start, to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels and be dangerous in transitions. I think we did that and it's been a different game to those where we conceded first."

stories.body:
Detroit Pistons center Jalen Duren will be out at least two weeks with a right hamstring strain, the team announced Sunday.

Duren suffered the injury in the first half of Friday's win over the Miami Heat. He played only 10 minutes before leaving the game.

Duren's offseason was marked by a lengthy standoff with the Pistons over a contract extension. He missed media day and the first few practices of training camp before ultimately signing a five-year, $200 million deal.

Last season, he averaged a career high in points (19.5 PPG), made his first All-Star team and was named to the All-NBA third team as the Pistons earned the top seed in the Eastern Conference. But he struggled mightily in the postseason, dropping to 10.2 points per game in 14 playoff games before Detroit's second-round exit.

Duren scored 22 points with nine rebounds in Detroit's season-opening win over the Boston Celtics.

Information from ESPN's Jamal Collier was used in this report.

stories.headline: Bruno Fernandes' home burgled during Man United loss against Como
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes returned from Italy after losing to Como with Manchester United in the early hours of Thursday morning and had to deal with a robbery at his house.
stories.body:
Police are investigating a burglary at Bruno Fernandes' home which took place as he returned from Italy with Manchester United after losing to Como.

Fernandes' family are understood not to have been in the house at the time and police quickly attended the scene, with United supporting their skipper.

A statement from Cheshire Police, given to ESPN, read: "At around 8.30 p.m. on Wednesday Oct. 21, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley.

"The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property.

"Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen.

"An investigation into the incident has been launched and enquiries are ongoing."

Detective Inspector David Jarvis of Macclesfield Proactive CID said: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible.

"As part of our enquiries were keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious.

"The same goes for anyone with any CCTV or dashcam footage which may aid the investigation."

Bruno Fernandes questions Man United tactics

A catastrophic night in Lombardy saw United suffer a humiliating 4-1 loss to Cesc Fabregas' side, which extended their winless run to seven fixtures and led to Fernandes publicly questioning the approach of boss Michael Carrick.

- Wayne Rooney: Bruno Fernandes, Man United players acting like 'babies'

- Who's to blame for Man United mess: Carrick, the players ... Ratcliffe?

- Cesc Fàbregas: I told Como players to 'slow down' in closing stages of Man United win

The result, alongside Fernandes' comments, had raised serious questions about Carrick's future ahead of Sunday's Premier League home game against Bournemouth, but he will remain in charge for that match, sources told ESPN.

United skipper Fernandes has been a pale imitation of last season's performer so far this term, and questioned Carrick's tactics as another Champions League trip ended with an eye-catching post-match player interview following on from last week's remarks by Lisandro Martínez.

Fernandes claimed it was the staff's decision "not to press man-to-man and sometimes leave a little bit of space in behind" in Como.

Information from ESPN's Rob Dawson, and the Press Association, contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Way-too-early AFL tiers: There's a clear flag favourite; 'silly season' winners and losers
stories.summary: Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL season is done and dusted, but that hasn't stopped ESPN's senior writer Jake Michaels from turning his attention to next year. Who are the 2027 flag favourites? Who are the legitimate contenders? And who should already be booking September holidays? It's our way-too-early edition of AFL tiers!

All of our best footy content, now on Instagram. Follow @espnfooty here!

Your new premiership favourite

1. HAWTHORN

Who knows if the Hawks would have been premiers this year if not for Hugh McCluggage's heroics late in that dramatic preliminary final at the MCG. There's certainly a real argument they would have gone all the way. This side, which is expertly coached by Sam Mitchell, just added Zach Merrett and Ben King to its best 23, two more experienced players desperate for flag success. There won't be many games the Hawks don't start favourite in next year. Even if this club's 2027 season over/under was set at preliminary final weekend, I'd still be taking the over.

Should be great, but there are some questions

2. BRISBANE

3. FREMANTLE

4. SYDNEY

The Lions just completed a remarkable three-peat and it certainly wouldn't have been outrageous for them to hold top spot here. But losing Lachie Neale and Chris Fagan -- arguably the two most important pieces of the club's modern-day dynasty -- cannot be underestimated. How do they fill those seismic gaps? The Dockers were the dominant team of the home and away season and if we played out the last four minutes of the Grand Final 100 times they probably win 99 of them. Instead, Fremantle has to spend all offseason dwelling on the greatest missed opportunity in club history. How do they respond in 2027? As for the Swans, who are always somewhere around the mark, nobody can really be sure what to expect after the Pullman Hotel saga. So many fascinating questions.

Silly season winners

5. GEELONG

6. WESTERN BULLDOGS

7. CARLTON

8. COLLINGWOOD

Each of these teams will be counting down the days until the 2027 season after drastically improving their lists during the trade and free agency window. The Cats landed the dynamic Toby Greene, significantly upgraded their ruck department with the singing of Rowan Marshall, and bolstered their defensive stocks with Jordan Ridley. The Bulldogs scored the biggest prize of all in Zak Butters, but they were also able to pry away Jordon Butts from the Crows, a much needed acquisition to what's been a shaky defence. The Blues will go into next season with Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield, and almost certainly father-son talent Cody Walker, while the Magpies added dual Brownlow medallist Lachie Neale and 2024 Coleman Medal winner Jesse Hogan.

Silly season losers

9. MELBOURNE

10. ADELAIDE

While a bunch of teams we'd expect to be in the fifth-to-10th range clearly improved their best 23, the Demons and Crows did nothing of the sort. Adelaide literally brought in nobody and will have to deal with the loss of key defender Jordon Butts, who departed as a free agent for the Bulldogs. Melbourne did sign several names, but do we think any of Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, and Bodie Ryan can be needle movers in 2027? But hey, these were two sides I was down on this year and both ultimately outperformed expectations. Perhaps they do have it all figured out...

It's now or never

11. GOLD COAST

12. NORTH MELBOURNE

13. ST KILDA

If not now, then when? The Suns rocketed to co-flag favouritism this time last year after signing Christian Petracca and Jamarra Ugle-Hagan. They ultimately won just nine games and finished 13th on the ladder. Disastrous. Damien Hardwick is under serious pressure to get more out of this list. Meanwhile, the Kangaroos haven't played finals in a decade, but there's some newfound optimism after the senior coaching appointment of highly regarded Jaymie Graham and the signing of Nick Blakey, the biggest name the club has attracted in a decade. The Saints also need to show something early in 2027 or Ross Lyon could be on his way out ... again! But the real worry is not doing enough to ensure star midfielder Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera signs on.

It's going to be another long year

14. PORT ADELAIDE

15. GWS

16. WEST COAST

17. RICHMOND

18. ESSENDON

Perhaps I'm being a tad harsh on Port, who were pretty competitive this year. But at the end of the day we're taking Zak Butters out of a side that won just seven games. The Giants lost four of their best players in Toby Greene, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield, and Kieren Briggs, and will be relying heavily on their younger talent next year. And then there's the Eagles, Tigers, and Bombers -- three teams that combined for just nine wins this year. We all expect these sides to be somewhere around the bottom of the ladder.

stories.headline: 'They wanted my undies': Chiefs embrace PNG welcome
stories.summary: Jarome Luai and Brian To'o were given a warm reception by their future home fans as they led Samoa to heavy thrashing of Papua New Guinea.
stories.body:
Jarome Luai wasn't left with much when he walked off the field in Port Moresby after helping lead Samoa to a World Cup demolition of Papua New Guinea on the ground he will call home in 12 months time.

"They wanted my undies too. I was like, nah, sorry, no can do," Luai told AAP after Saturday's 64-6 win.

The Kumuls were well beaten by a Samoan side stacked with NRL talent, including Luai and international teammate Brian To'o who will both join the PNG Chiefs in 2028.

But the scoreline fails to tell you how inhospitable the crowd was at the National Football Stadium, where for the first 40 minutes Samoa were up against it.

Supporters unfurled banners before kick-off with messages for Luai and To'o.

And when the Samoan players threw their jersey or shorts into the crowd at fulltime they were showered with bilum bags and knitted hats in return.

"I saw on the board there was 15,000 people but bro, that was probably one of the biggest atmospheres I've ever played in," said To'o, who scored a try in Port Moresby after signing his Chiefs deal before he had even visited the country.

"You can't explain the energy, (it felt like) a grand final they definitely brought a vibe.

"I felt so emotional this week, seeing the lifestyle people have here - they don't have everything but footy means so much to them.

"I saw how much it meant for the kids just to see me in person, that's something that I'm really looking forward to in 2028 to give them all that hope and a bit of joy as well.

"They definitely brought a smile to my face, so hopefully, I did the same for them."

To'o will see out the 2027 season with Penrith before linking with the Chiefs, while Luai become a Parramatta player on a one-year come November 1 after being shown the door by Wests Tigers.

The five-eighth likened the challenge of playing against a PNG home crowd to a State of Origin match for NSW at Suncorp Stadium as he went toe to toe with Gairo Voro - the homegrown No. 6 who has been likened to Luai.

"It's my first time playing in PNG and that was an amazing experience in itself so it gives you a sense of what it's going to be like in 2028 now," Luai said.

"The best way we could show respect to the Kumuls is play our hardest, the PNG boys have a lot of ticker and I told Gairo I can't wait to play with him in the future."

Samoa returned to Sydney on Sunday where they will face Tonga in a week's time with the winner of the pool stage match set to top Group B/C.
